Make your celebration a success by keeping these tips in mind: - Communicate early: Share your HR calendar at the beginning of the year to give employees plenty of notice about upcoming engagement holidays so they can plan accordingly. - Accommodate all teams and time zones: If your team is distributed, make sure your holiday activities aren’t exclusively offered to your onsite staff or a specific timezone. - Keep a company calendar: Use a shared calendar or scheduling software to track holidays, making it easy for employees to see upcoming company events. - Include employees in planning: Ask your employees what holidays they'd like to celebrate, and foster an environment where team members feel empowered to organize their engagement activities. Promoting holidays and encouraging work-life balance is crucial to keep a motivated and engaged workforce. With these tips in mind, you can create a more supportive and connected work environment. Year-round activities to boost employee engagement Employee engagement holidays aren’t the only opportunities to bring your employees together. Here are some other year-round activities to create highly engaged employees and create a positive work environment: - Social gatherings: Plan regular social events throughout or after the workday, such as virtual coffee breaks, happy hours, communal lunches, and more. - Birthday and anniversary celebrations: Don't save the recognition just for National Employee Appreciation Day. Celebrate your employees' birthdays and work anniversaries with small gifts, words of appreciation, or other gestures to show employee appreciation. - Employee-led interest groups or ERGs: Encourage employees to create and lead clubs or Employee Resource Groups ( ERGs ) based on their shared interests, characteristics, and identities. - Wellness challenges: Plan company wellness challenges outside of Mental Health Awareness Month. Step-count competitions, healthy eating, mindfulness, and gratitude challenges can all help to boost employees' well-being. - Lunch and Learns: Host regular " Lunch and Learn " sessions where employees can learn from their colleagues, leadership teams, or outside speakers. ‍ You don’t need to wait for a holiday to celebrate your team. Activities and traditions like these can demonstrate your commitment to fostering engagement and morale in the workplace year-round. Frequently Asked Questions What is an employee engagement calendar? An Employee Engagement Calendar is a structured schedule of activities and events designed to boost employee morale, encourage collaboration, and strengthen employee relationships and company culture. Why is an employee engagement calendar important for your organization? An Employee Engagement Calendar is essential to promote a positive work environment, improve employee satisfaction and team spirit, and increase retention rates. Employee engagement activities create a sense of belonging, enhance productivity, and build stronger relationships among team members. How many events should you plan a year? There's no one-size-fits-all answer to how often you should plan events. It depends on your budget, objectives, and the unique dynamics of your team. However, as a general guideline, planning at least one event per quarter can help maintain momentum and keep morale high throughout the year. July 24, 2026 Table of contents As a managed marketplace, we don’t just partner with the best vendors to provide the products and services on our platform. We also take active measures to ensure your event will run smoothly and to your satisfaction. To ensure that you have the best experience, all of our vendors and experiences go through a comprehensive vetting process . In the rare case that an issue is experienced during an event, we have this Happiness Guarantee Policy in place to protect both our customer and vendor communities and to effectively investigate and resolve the dispute. Sharing your feedback Regardless of whether it’s positive or constructive, your feedback is super important to us! This is why we will always send you a form where you can share your thoughts regarding your recent experience within 24 hours of your event taking place. If you rank your experience 2 or less stars out of 5 stars on any criteria and specify that you would like to receive follow-up communication regarding your recent experience, one of our Account Managers will reach out to you to collect more information and investigate the situation. Our investigation procedure Whenever a customer submits feedback rating us 2 or below out of 5 stars, our team carefully analyzes the details provided and conducts a mutual investigation with the host(s) or vendor(s) involved. In order to make sure that each one of our customers will always be satisfied with our service, even in cases of dissatisfaction from an event, we hold onto your event fees for 3 days following your event, before transferring them to the vendor(s). In cases where a dispute was found justified, either fully or partially, this allows us to make a full or partial refund of your event fees. Since we all know there are two sides to every story, it is up to our team to determine how the responsibility for your dissatisfaction falls between the different parties involved in your event, and as a result, whether compensation is due and to which. Making things right As a thank you for your honest feedback and an apology for your unmet expectations, we are happy to offer a complimentary experience to help re-write your memory with us. Depending on the headcount of your original event, you can choose from a list of the following experiences: Coworker Clash Trivia Jeoparty Escape Quest Mini Games Pictionary Taboo Charades Bootcamp Class Boom Box Topdog Trivia If you would prefer to receive a full refund instead, one of our Account Managers will send you a second form to collect additional feedback from your event attendees. In order to qualify for the refund, at least 3 people or 10% of participants (whichever is greater) must provide feedback. If their collective score is 2 or less, we’ll refund your money back, no questions asked. We’ve got your back! Our Happiness Guarantee Policy is a risk-free way to have fun. Although we hope every event you book with us turns out to be a blast 🚀 and that you’ll never have to take advantage of the policy, you can book with confidence and rest easy knowing it’s there! Either way, we promise you’ll have a smooth and seamless experience. Try out one of our virtual experiences and see for yourself! ✨ Did this answer your question? March 10, 2026 Table of contents 🛡️Quality You Can Trust: Our Expert Vetting Process As a managed marketplace where about half of our experiences are made end-to-end in house, we understand that the quality of our vendors is the bread and butter of our core offering. We choose only the best vendors who are at the top of their field of expertise to supply the products and services offered on our platform. Our dedicated Vendor Operations Managers carefully source and vet each vendor before on-boarding them, so that you don’t have to. 👀 What We Look For Across all vendors and hosts, we evaluate: Customer service & human interaction skills: Professionalism, responsiveness, and the ability to create a welcoming environment. Quality of product or experience: Premium materials, polished content, and smooth execution. Proven experience & credibility: Demonstrated expertise and real-world track record. Coachability & willingness to improve: Openness to feedback, iteration, and collaboration. 📦 Kit Vendor Vetting All external vendors - including those providing physical kits - go through multiple layers of review. 1. Legal & Compliance Screening Every potential vendor undergoes compliance checks, including: OFAC sanctions list verification to confirm the vendor or individual does not appear on applicable sanctions lists Location compliance verification to ensure vendors operate in countries aligned with data protection and internet security best practices While these checks rarely surface issues, they are a required safeguard. 2. Due Diligence & Credibility Review We begin with comprehensive due diligence: Reviewing websites and public-facing materials Assessing brand credibility and experience Evaluating existing client feedback and reputation 3. Product & Experience Testing We review performance materials and demo the experience ourselves prior to promoting the experience. For kit vendors, we require a physical sample kit. Our team: Tests functionality and usability Evaluates product quality Reviews packaging and presentation Confirms the kit performs as intended for a Confetti event setting If it doesn’t meet our standards, it doesn’t immediately move forward. We will work with the vendor to adjust the kit as we see fit or decide we no longer want to move forward with the kit. 4. Initial Event Review As a final step, we validate kit performance and feedback through the first live client event conducted via Confetti. To move forward, the vendor must receive positive feedback, deliver the product to our standards of quality, and complete an overall successful experience. We will also work with the vendor to adjust content based on feedback or experience. 🎤 Confetti Originals & Partner Host Vetting Confetti Originals are built in-house, and they are led by carefully selected professional hosts. Legal & Compliance Screening Every potential host undergoes compliance checks, including: OFAC sanctions list verification to confirm the vendor or individual does not appear on applicable sanctions lists Location compliance verification to ensure vendors operate in countries aligned with data protection and internet security best practices While these checks rarely surface issues, they are a required safeguard. 2. Performance & Presence Evaluation We assess: Public speaking or performance background Acting, presenting, or live facilitation experience Ability to command a (virtual) room with confidence and warmth Engagement style and adaptability We’re not just looking for someone who can talk. We’re looking for someone who can lead! 3. Technical Competency Review Running a seamless experience requires more than charisma. Hosts must: Demonstrate comfort with virtual platforms Meet technical setup requirements Navigate technical tools or accompanying kits confidently Handle essential functions independently (recording, screen sharing, troubleshooting basics) 4. Structured Onboarding & SLAs Approved hosts complete detailed onboarding covering: Customer satisfaction standards Service-level expectations Process requirements Brand alignment 5. Shadowing & Final Sign-Off Every new host is shadowed during their first live experiences. According to research, 65% of employees are happy with their job. While that’s a majority of the workforce, it is concerning that the remaining 35% don’t feel the same way. Happy employees tend to perform better at work; they’re more productive and engaged in their responsibilities, while disengaged employees can drag down company profits by 15% or more. ‍ While no workforce is immune to the occasional dissatisfied worker, it becomes a serious issue if the problem spreads to the majority of a department or — even worse — the entire company. Retaining key employees may become nearly impossible, resulting in lots of time (and money) spent hiring and training new workers. When your workers are disengaged, you will likely deal with more HR complaints, and team members may be unwilling to collaborate with one another. If you are noticing these and other common signs of dissatisfaction, it’s time to nip the problem in the bud. While it may take some time to right the ship, you’ll be glad you made the effort. Get in Touch See Ideas Table of Contents Defining Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion FAQ Ready to strengthen team connections? Contact us to get started. Get in Touch What is employee engagement? 🤔 Employee engagement measures the satisfaction people receive from their roles . Engaged employees feel a sense of pride in their work; they believe they’re contributing to the company's mission and success. They generally feel high levels of motivation to perform well in their position and will make additional efforts to ensure they handle their responsibilities properly. An engaged employee collaborates well with their team members. They’ll take action when they see areas for improvement that could benefit the company. Engaged workers are eager to assume new responsibilities and are often the first to volunteer to help with major projects. When you have an engaged employee, you know you can trust them to get things done. The following are some of the ways employees show engagement: Producing high-grade, quality work on the regular Providing suggestions to improve company processes Going the extra mile to ensure new workers assimilate into the organization Voicing their opinion on new company initiatives Participating in company-sponsored events outside of work Usually, it’s quite easy to identify engaged workers.
